name: Azacitidine
drug_class: Hypomethylating agent (DNA methyltransferase inhibitor); pyrimidine nucleoside analogue
route_note: SC or IV for 7 days every 28 days; oral tablets (Onureg) for AML maintenance — not interchangeable
originator: Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences (František Šorm, Alois Pískala); developed by Pharmion
owner: Bristol Myers Squibb (Vidaza, Onureg); generic injectable (many)

discovery.by: Alois Pískala and František Šorm, Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry, Prague
discovery.note: Synthesised as a cytotoxic nucleoside; its DNA-demethylating activity at low doses was recognised around 1980.

tagline: First drug approved for myelodysplastic syndromes; a DNA demethylating nucleoside
summary: Azacitidine is a cytidine analogue that is incorporated into RNA and DNA; in DNA it traps and degrades DNA methyltransferases, reversing aberrant gene silencing. It was the first drug to extend survival in higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes and, with venetoclax, is a standard for older or unfit patients with acute myeloid leukaemia.
mechanism: Azacitidine is phosphorylated and mainly incorporated into RNA, disrupting protein synthesis; a fraction is reduced to the deoxy form and incorporated into DNA.

In DNA the 5-aza ring forms covalent adducts with DNA methyltransferase 1, depleting the enzyme so that newly synthesised DNA loses methylation. This can reactivate silenced tumour-suppressor genes, promote differentiation and trigger viral-mimicry interferon responses; higher concentrations are directly cytotoxic.
uses: Myelodysplastic syndromes (all FAB subtypes in US label)
Acute myeloid leukaemia in unfit patients (with venetoclax, or alone)
Oral azacitidine: maintenance in AML in first remission

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Pískala and Šorm synthesise 5-azacytidine in Prague.

history.title: Demethylation discovered
history.detail: Jones and Taylor show 5-azacytidine inhibits DNA methylation and induces cell differentiation.

history.title: CALGB 9221
history.detail: Silverman et al. report azacitidine improves response and quality of life in MDS.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Vidaza (Pharmion), the first drug for MDS.

history.title: Celgene acquisition
history.detail: Celgene acquires Pharmion; EU approval follows in December.

history.title: AZA-001
history.detail: Fenaux et al. show azacitidine prolongs overall survival in higher-risk MDS.

history.title: Oral azacitidine and VIALE-A
history.detail: Onureg approved for AML maintenance (QUAZAR AML-001); VIALE-A establishes venetoclax plus azacitidine for unfit AML.

history.title: JMML
history.detail: FDA approves azacitidine for juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia.

facts: Decitabine is the closely related deoxy analogue that is incorporated only into DNA.
